definition_audit.name: comparatorRegret
definition_audit.audit: 0-based range T replaces source 1..T via ell_candidate(t)=ell_source(t+1). Arbitrary type X generalizes V subset R^d. Formula does not itself enforce prediction membership in V. At T=0 both sums vanish.

definition_audit.name: NoRegret
definition_audit.audit: For each fixed u in V and positive epsilon, eventually regret/T<=epsilon. This only encodes upper-asymptotic behavior, with no existence of a finite real limit. Printed display says lim, while prose says at most sublinear. Preserve this delta without approving a textual repair.

binders.delta: fixed comparator matches source; epsilon/eventual formulation is a reinterpretation of at-most-sublinear, not literal ordinary-limit statement

definition_audit.name: empiricalMean
definition_audit.audit: For n>0 arithmetic mean agrees after reindexing. At n=0 Lean division gives 0. Source never asserts mean argmin uniqueness at empty horizon; this extension cannot be sold as such characterization.

binders.delta: [0,1] only at use sites; n=0 extension

definition_audit.name: meanPredict
definition_audit.audit: Candidate t=0 uses 1/2, matching source x_1=0.5, and t>0 uses mean of prior t observations. Broader p15 algorithm permits any first prediction, whereas candidate correctly specializes Theorem 1.3.

definition_audit.name: squaredBestRegret
definition_audit.audit: Uses sInf of loss image over [0,1], where source uses min. Need nonempty bounded-below image and attained minimum equivalence; squared losses provide relevant structure but no implementation proof inspected. Source mean characterization is only for legal y and positive T; at T=0 image is {0}, with all comparators minimizers.

definition_audit.name: LimitNoRegret
definition_audit.audit: For every fixed u in V, exists finite a<=0 with regret/T tending to a. Encodes literal ordinary-real-limit reading. Does not assert uniform convergence in u, convergence of worst-comparator regret, or probability mode.

principal_findings: The four candidates are absent as theorems and proofs on the inspected source pages. They are candidate-derived obligations.
The source contains an ordinary lim no-regret display but only a finite upper-regret bound proof. No ordinary-limit existence derivation is printed.
Theorem 1.3's 4+4 ln T controls best-comparator regret from above. Neither an exact-zero normalized limit nor arbitrary-comparator ordinary-limit existence follows from that upper bound alone.
Dyadic recurrence, subsequence counts/limits, mean-convergence equivalence and obstruction are not source statements in this bounded packet.
No EXCESS hypothesis found in the four supplied signatures after expanding all supplied project definitions. This bounded observation does not certify source equivalence or proof correctness.
Mean/argmin characterization needs positive prefix length and legal observations; T=0 extensions are explicit and cannot imply source uniqueness.

standing_assumptions.content: Source general game V subset R^d, x_t in V, ell_t:V->R, fixed u in V; prediction superset W is only a footnoted variant.
Scalar game observations y_t in [0,1]; arbitrary pathwise stream; adversary may observe current prediction before choosing y_t; no i.i.d., filtration or event premise.
Past y_i are known when predicting; meanPredict uses only prior observations. The generic loss-observation protocol is not fully specified on these pages and is not invented.
Source uses t=1..T and positive T; sealed definitions use t=0..T-1 and permit T=0. Infinite sequences are natural extensions needed for limits, not additional stochastic assumptions.
